Subject: Orchid QBR prep — health snapshot, renewal risk register, and CTO docket

Team / Maya —

Attaching the working pulse deck and the renewal-risk register for Orchid's Q3 QBR. Goal for this thread: lock the executive attention items (1 slide), confirm mitigation owners for top 3 risks, and agree a short scope for a performance deep-dive with engineering.

Quick summary (please scan):
- Health: product usage up ~18% month-over-month; embedding calls have spiked and are now ~42% of token volume.
- Renewal: renewal date 2028-09-15; current committed ARR: $1.2M.
- Risks: (A) Latency spikes on long-context prompt paths, (B) Token run rate mismatch vs forecast (cost overrun potential), (C) Data residency ask from legal that may require Private deployment.

Asks (owners / deadlines):
- Provide 1-line exec flag for each risk (Laura) — due Thu EOD 6/27.
- Grace to attach the usage delta table + known quota events for last 90 days — due Wed 6/26 noon.
- Stephanie to draft one-slide CTO docket with impact numbers (latency, cost delta, mitigations, one recommended ask: 60-day pilot for dedicated pool) — due Fri 6/28 10:00am.
- Maya / Orchid: can you confirm the list of internal stakeholders who should be on the deep-dive (eng + infra)? A 30–45m window next week would be ideal.

Attachments: QBR_PulseDeck_v2.pdf (working), renewal-risk-register_Orchid.xlsx (live register).

Notes on mitigation options we should be prepared to brief: quantization & dynamic batching for the top-10 heavy prompts; suggest a short A/B on lower-precision variant where quality permits; routing policy to burst to Dedicated if latency SLO threatened.

Maya — feel free to reply inline with any missing facts.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake

Thanks Jordan — useful summary. A few quick reality checks from our side: we definitely want the deep-dive on latency and cost before the QBR.

- Stakeholders: I'll pull in Priya (Infra), Lucas (ML Eng), and Sarah (Security). Daniel is on the thread for billing questions.
- Latency: we've seen spikes on >4k token conversations; they correlate with a new prompt set we rolled on 6/03. The spikes are mostly in our EU region customers although we operate from a US primary endpoint.
- Cost: embeddings went up after the prompt change; our procurement team is worried about the 30% increase in monthly run-rate.
- Data residency: legal wants a path to guarantee logs never leave EU for a subset of traffic. We're not asking for full Private yet, but want options and a ballpark for cost delta.

For the deep-dive, we can do Tue 7/2 10:30–11:15 PT or Wed 7/3 09:00–09:45 PT. Which works for Redwood engineering?

On the deck: please include a slide that shows token composition (generation vs embedding vs system prompts) — that helped previously.

Maya

Adding the data slice I promised — high level here, I'll drop the csv to the Drive folder in a few minutes.

Highlights:
- 90d token trend: +18% overall, embeddings +42%, chat gen +11%.
- Top 5 prompts (50% of tokens) are all embedding-heavy; those are the biggest cost levers.
- Latency distribution: median 120ms, 95th 880ms; 95th is driven by long-context (>4k) requests and EU routing fallbacks.

Proposed mitigations (short list):
1) Enable prefix KV caching for the top-5 embedding flows (low friction).
2) Trial a 16-bit quantized variant for embeddings on a dedicated pool (measure quality delta on test set).
3) Configure routing policy to prefer nearest region endpoints and fall back less aggressively to US.

I'll upload the usage delta table (usage_delta_orchid_90d.csv) to the Drive link referenced in the thread.

- Grace
Product Ops | Redwood Inference

Jordan / team —

Nice progress. For the exec docket, I'm proposing we surface three concise flags (one-liners) that will be read by our CRO + CTO ahead of the QBR. Draft below — please edit if you disagree: 

1) Latency: "95th percentile latency elevated in EU due to long-context prompt set; recommend 6-week dedicated-pool pilot to reduce tail latency and quantify quality trade-offs."
2) Cost: "Embedding-heavy prompt changes have increased token spend ~30% month-over-month; recommend targeted quantization + prefix caching pilot to reduce embedding unit cost by 20–30%."
3) Compliance: "Customer requests EU-only log residency for a subset of traffic; evaluate Private deployment feasibility and cost delta for scoped subset by QBR."

Action items to close before exec readout:
- Jordan: compile the one-slide exec summary with the three flags and 1–2 bullets of impact each — due Fri 6/28 3pm PT.
- Grace: confirm measured 95th etc and attach test cases for the pilot — due Thu 6/27 EOD.
- Stephanie: finalize pilot ask economics and recommended gating metrics — due Fri 6/28 10am PT.

Once we have that one-slide, I'll route it to CRO/CTO inbox with the recommended next steps and suggested brief attendees. Good work.
